text: durlabha mānava-janma labhiyā saṁsāre
kṛṣṇa nā bhajinu duḥkha kahiba kāhāre?
translation: The human form of life is the rarest opportunity for attaining spiritual perfection. Now I am lamenting because I’ve somehow or other been born with such an opportunity, but I wasted it by never worshiping Lord Kṛṣṇa. O, to whom shall I tell the tale of this misery?

text: ‘saṁsāra’ ‘saṁsāra’ kari’ michhe gela kāla
lābha nā ha-ila kichhu, ghaṭila jañjāla
translation: Having married and entered into the entanglements of materialistic family life, I passed my time in vain. I never got any tangible gain or permanent benefit, only trouble and botheration.

text: kisera saṁsāra ei chhāyābāji prāya
ihāte mamatā kari vṛthā dina yāya
translation: What kind of world is this anyway? It seems to be just like a magic lantern show that I saw at a carnival, wherein so many shadows and optical illusions dance magically before my eyes. I feel great attachment and identification with such a world, and thus day after day passes by fruitlessly, without any purpose whatsoever.

text: e deha patana ha’le ki rabe āmāra?
keha sukha nāhi dibe putra paribāra
translation: When this body drops dead on the ground, then what will remain mine? At that moment, all of my sons and dearest loved ones will not be able to give me any happiness.

text: gardabhera mata āmi kari pariśrama
kāra lāgi’ eta kari, nā ghuchila bhrama
translation: I work hard just like an ass every day, and now I am wondering for whom am I working so hard? I am still surrounded by so many illusions.

text: dina yāya michhā kāje, niśā nidrā-vaśe
nāhi bhāvi maraṇa nikaṭe āchhe vase
translation: I waste every day in useless, insignificant work, and I waste every night controlled by sleep. And in every twenty-four hours I never for one second consider that death is sitting very close by my side.

text: bhāla manda khāi, heri, pari, chintā-hīna
nāhi bhāvi, e deha chhāḍiba kona dina
translation: I live a very carefree life-style, eating, going out, wearing nice clothes, as I please, but I never consider that one day I will have to give up this body.

text: deha-geha-kalatrādi-chintā avirata
jāgichhe hṛdaye mora buddhi kari hata
translation: My poor heart is plagued by constant anxieties about the maintenance and daily turmoils created by my body, my house, my wife, my family members, and my social obligations. All these anxieties are pinching me and destroying all my intelligence.

text: hāya, hāya! nāhi bhāvi – anitya e saba
jīvana vigate kothā rahibe vaibhava?
translation: Alas, alas! What a remorseful situation has arisen! I am absorbed in all this trouble, but I never consider that all these things are temporary and subject to perish very soon. After I’m dead and gone, where will all of my material opulences remain?

text: śmaśāne śarīra mama paḍiyā rahibe
vihaṅga-pataṅga tāya vihāra karibe
translation: When my body will be thrown in the pit at the cremation grounds, it will simply lie there motionlessly. Then many crows, vultures, ants, and worms will come and playfully sport there.

text: kukkura sṛgāla saba ānandita ha’ye
mahotsava karibe āmāra deha la’ye
translation: All the stray dogs and jackals will then become very much delighted, and in great ecstasy they will make a festival ground out of my body and will have a huge celebration and feast.

text: ye dehera ei gati, tāra anugata
saṁsāra-vaibhava āra bandhu-jana yata
translation: Just see, this is the ultimate destination of this material body. And the most amazing thing is that all of my material opulences, house, family and friends have exactly the same destination.

text: ataeva māyā-moha chhāḍi buddhimāna
nitya-tattva kṛṣṇa-bhakti karuna sandhāna
translation: Therefore I ask of anyone who has any sharp intelligence: please give up all of these temporary illusions presented by Māyā, and kindly search after the means to get pure devotion to Lord Kṛṣṇa, for this is the only really tangible eternal truth.
